titulo: Handwriting Might Have Identified Famous Byzantine Artist

fuente.nota: Text shortened by removing paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: The artist Giotto who lived in Italy about 700 years ago is often considered the father of Western painting. But at the same time that Giotto lived, Manuel Panselinos was equally important to a different tradition: the art of Byzantium.
The art of Byzantium can be found in Eastern Orthodox churches across Greece, Serbia and other Orthodox countries. Byzantium is an ancient name for the modern city of Istanbul.

Nothing is known of Panselinos’ life. Historians now believe Panselinos was a nickname. They now suspect his real name was likely Ioannis Astrapas. He was from the northern Greek city of Thessaloniki.

Work said to be made by Panselinos, from the late 1200s and early 1300s, is considered the finest produced in the Byzantine empire. That ancient empire covered parts of Europe and Asia. It lasted from the fall of the Roman Empire until the capture of the capital Constantinople by the Ottoman Turks in 1453.
Art historians had long suspected that “Panselinos” could have been a nickname, or a pseudonym, for a member of the Macedonian School of painting in Thessaloniki. The name means “full moon” in Greek.

Now handwriting expert Christina Sotirakoglou has found new evidence. She matched lettering on a document thought to be by Astrapas with writing on a church painting at Mount Athos in northern Greece. The Protaton church painting has been considered Panselinos’ best work.

Father Cosmas Simonopetritis is a former administrator at Mount Athos; the religious community is where the Protaton church stands. He said Sotirakoglou’s and his own research “clearly prove” Panselinos’ real identity.

Constantinos Vafiadis is a professor of Byzantine art who was not involved in the research. Vafiadis said he found strong points in the nickname theory and naming Astrapas as the true artist. However, he added that it appeared more than one painter had created the art at the Protaton church.

“I agree with attributing part of the paintings to Ioannis Astrapas,” Vafiadis said. “But again there remains much ground for future research into that person, because other Mount Athos monuments from the same period have not yet been sufficiently published.”

“Panselinos” and his fellow artists at the time are linked with a rebirth in Eastern Orthodox art. Their work brought back forms and skills inherited from ancient times. Facial expressions got a deeper humanity, and greater attention was paid to proportion and depth of field in composition.

The trail started with linking Astrapas to the person who wrote a book called the Marcian Codex GR 516 from the early 1300s. The book contains artwork and is handwritten in Greek. Among the painted pictures, or illustrations, is a full moon.

With a name found for the person who produced the manuscript, the next step was to compare it to the writing on the painting in the Protaton church that has been traditionally linked with “Panselinos.”
“I was forced to study the Protato paintings based on photographs,” Sotirakoglou told the AP. Sotirakoglou works as a court expert who examines handwriting in criminal cases.

“It’s a Phi that stands out, and is similar” in both the manuscript and the Protato painting, she said. “Matches also followed with other letters, T, with its proportions, which is bigger, covering the other letters and is topped with a curve, the proportions of the K.”
“That’s where my desire was born...to explore the mystery around the name and the identity of Panselinos,” he said, adding that he thinks the artist has now gotten “his true identity.”
titulo_es: Handwriting might have identified a famous Byzantine painter
resumen_es: A Greek handwriting expert has compared the writing in a manuscript with that of some wall paintings on Mount Athos and claims that Panselinos, the great Byzantine painter of around 1300, was in fact Ioannis Astrapas.

ideas_clave.idea: Manuel Panselinos was as significant for Byzantine art, still found in Orthodox churches, as his contemporary Giotto was for Western painting.
Nothing is known about his life; his works from around 1300 are considered the best of the Byzantine empire, and scholars have long believed 'Panselinos', meaning 'full moon', was a pseudonym.

A handwriting expert has matched the lettering of a document attributed to Ioannis Astrapas with the inscriptions on the Protaton church paintings at Mount Athos, and a former Athos administrator considers the identity proven.
An independent professor finds the theory convincing but believes several painters worked on the church and calls for more research.
These artists led a revival in Orthodox art, recovering ancient techniques and giving faces more humanity and compositions better proportion and depth.
The investigation began by linking Astrapas to an illustrated Greek manuscript containing a full moon, and then comparing its script with the Protaton inscriptions.

Working from photographs, the expert, who normally analyses handwriting in criminal cases, found matching letters, and the researcher who started the inquiry believes the artist has finally regained his true identity.

resumen_modelo: The text reports that a famous Byzantine painter may finally have been identified. Manuel Panselinos, who worked around 1300 and is regarded as the Byzantine counterpart of Giotto, produced some of the finest art of the empire, yet nothing is known about his life, and historians have long suspected that his name, meaning 'full moon', was a nickname. Now a Greek handwriting expert has compared the script of a manuscript attributed to Ioannis Astrapas, a painter from Thessaloniki, with the inscriptions on the Protaton church paintings at Mount Athos, considered Panselinos' masterpiece, and found clear similarities. While one of the researchers believes the identity has been proven, an independent professor, although broadly convinced, argues that several artists worked on the church and that further research is needed. The text also stresses that these painters revived classical techniques and brought greater humanity to Orthodox art.

preguntas.pregunta: Who is often considered the father of Western painting?
preguntas.cita: The artist Giotto who lived in Italy about 700 years ago is often considered the father of Western painting.
preguntas.explicacion: Giotto is the father of Western painting. Panselinos (probably Astrapas) was just as important, but for the Byzantine tradition; Vafiadis is a present-day professor.

preguntas.pregunta: When did the Byzantine empire end, according to the text?
opciones: With the fall of the Roman Empire
When the Ottoman Turks captured Constantinople in 1453
respuestas: When the Ottoman Turks captured Constantinople in 1453
preguntas.cita: It lasted from the fall of the Roman Empire until the capture of the capital Constantinople by the Ottoman Turks in 1453.
preguntas.explicacion: The empire ended with the fall of Constantinople in 1453. The fall of Rome marks its beginning, the late 13th century is Panselinos’s period and Thessaloniki is not presented as the capital.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 4 a word that means “a false name used by an artist or writer”.

preguntas.cita: could have been a nickname, or a pseudonym
preguntas.explicacion: “Pseudonym” (es: seudónimo); a “nickname” is an informal name (es: apodo). The initial “p” is silent.

preguntas.pregunta: What did Christina Sotirakoglou compare to find new evidence?
opciones: The colours used in two church paintings
The lettering on a document and the writing on a church painting
respuestas: The lettering on a document and the writing on a church painting
preguntas.cita: She matched lettering on a document thought to be by Astrapas with writing on a church painting at Mount Athos
preguntas.explicacion: She compared the handwriting in a document attributed to Astrapas with the letters in a painting in the Protaton. She did not analyse colours or birth records, and there are no photographs of Panselinos.

preguntas.explicacion: Vafiadis accepts attributing part of the paintings to Astrapas, but believes that more than one painter was involved.

preguntas.pregunta: Why does Vafiadis think more research is needed?
respuestas: Because other monuments at Mount Athos from the same period have not yet been sufficiently published, so there is still much to learn about Astrapas before drawing firm conclusions.
preguntas.cita: other Mount Athos monuments from the same period have not yet been sufficiently published
preguntas.explicacion: The answer must point out that there is no published documentation on other monuments of the same period on Mount Athos.

preguntas.explicacion: “Rebirth” means a renewal or revival; synonyms: “revival”, “renaissance”.

preguntas.pregunta: Which change in Orthodox art is associated with Panselinos and his contemporaries?
opciones: Faces gained deeper humanity and compositions more attention to proportion and depth
They replaced religious subjects with landscapes
They abandoned techniques inherited from ancient times
respuestas: Faces gained deeper humanity and compositions more attention to proportion and depth
preguntas.cita: Facial expressions got a deeper humanity, and greater attention was paid to proportion and depth of field in composition.
preguntas.explicacion: Faces became more human and composition gained proportion and depth. In fact, ancient techniques were recovered, not abandoned, and the text does not talk about landscapes.

preguntas.explicacion: Among the illustrations in the codex there is a full moon, a relevant detail because “Panselinos” means “full moon”.

respuestas: She found a distinctive letter Phi that is similar in the manuscript and the painting, as well as matching features in other letters, such as the large T topped with a curve and the proportions of the K.
